subject: Cygnus RFP - attestation queue, ingress/egress data-flow clarifications
messages:
From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@cygnusbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procure-cygnus@cygnusbank.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Cygnus RFP - data-flow & attestation questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick submission last week. Our security team reviewed the initial packet and has three immediate clarifications before we move the RFP to the legal/procurement review: 

1) We need a concise diagram and explanation of how data enters and leaves Redwood's hosted inference pipeline (ingress/egress), specifically for streaming generation endpoints.
2) Please confirm whether token-level request logs (not model outputs) are retained and for how long; if retained, provide the retention policy artifact.
3) We saw a control gap note about third-party telemetry in the draft – can you surface any compensating controls or an exception/mitigation log?

If you can provide a short packet (diagram + one-page answers + evidence pointers) by next Friday (5/21), that will keep things on schedule.

Appreciate it,
Elaine
Elaine Turner
Senior Security Analyst, Cygnus Bank
elaine.turner@cygnusbank.com

--
Attachment: none (initial request)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@cygnusbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>; procure-cygnus@cygnusbank.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cygnus RFP - data-flow & attestation questions

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver what you requested; proposed plan below and a couple quick clarifying Qs.

Plan (deliver by 2027-05-21):
- network-dataflow-diagram.pdf (visual: request path, preprocessing, KV cache, model variant, response path, external storage)
- control-mapping-v2.xlsx (mapping of SOC 2/ISO controls to evidence artifacts + links)
- one-page answers to the three bullets (in-line in the Drive folder)
- ingress-egress-exception-log.csv (current exceptions & compensating controls)

Clarifying Qs:
- For the streaming endpoints, do you want sequence-level diagramming (client -> load balancer -> inference router -> GPU pool -> response) or a higher-level flow? We'll include both but can emphasize whichever you prefer.
- Regarding retention: would an outline of logs (types + TTL) plus the KMS key lifecycle document suffice, or do you want redacted sample logs?

I'll tag Karthik for SOC 2 mapping and Jonas for the network diagram. If that plan works I'll start assembling and share a Drive folder link by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments: none yet

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cygnus RFP - data-flow & attestation questions

Irene — quick internal note while I put the diagram together.

- For streaming flows, I'll produce two layers: a simple lane diagram for auditors and a technical swimlane for Cygnus' infra team (includes LB config, TLS termination points, and KV cache invalidation triggers).
- On the exception log: we have three historic exceptions relevant to external telemetry (all low/medium risk) — will include timestamps, root cause, compensating control, and closure status. My plan is to redact any PII from sample artifacts.
- Karthik: please confirm the SOC 2 control IDs we should surface for token-level logging and for key rotation (I think CC6.2-ish in our internal mapping).

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachment: network-dataflow-diagram.pdf (draft v0.3)

From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@cygnusbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procure-cygnus@cygnusbank.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cygnus RFP - data-flow & attestation questions

Thanks, team. A couple follow-ups after an internal read-through: 

1) The swimlane looks good; for our reviewers we also need a short statement on whether request metadata (IP, timestamp, user-agent) is considered telemetry vs. logs that would be produced under a subpoena. Clarify retention and access controls.
2) The exception CSV is useful — can you add a column indicating whether the exception required an operator change vs code change vs config?

One operational ask: if you can provide a short script or CLI command (redacted) showing how to export a redacted timestamped event from your request logs that would be a big help to our investigators. If that's not appropriate, a step-by-step export playbook is fine.

We still target legal review next week pending these items.

Best,
Elaine

--
On Thu, May 13, 2027 at 08:22 Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Irene — quick internal note while I put the diagram together.

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@cygnusbank.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cygnus RFP - data-flow & attestation questions

Elaine — final package attached and next steps below. Thanks for the precise follow-ups; we've incorporated them.

What we delivered (attached + Drive links):
- network-dataflow-diagram.pdf (final v0.6) — both high-level and swimlane layers included.
- control-mapping-v2.xlsx — SOC 2 & ISO mappings, with direct links to artifacts.
- ingress-egress-exception-log.csv — added operator/code/config classification and closure status.
- export-playbook.md (Drive link) — redacted CLI examples and an auditor playbook for exporting redacted request-event records.

Quick answers to your inline asks:
- Request metadata (IP, timestamp, UA) is classified as operational logs in our taxonomy. Access is restricted to SRE and security-ops; exports require a documented ASR (artifact sharing request) and internal approver (Security Manager). Retention is 90 days for request logs; aggregated telemetry (metrics) retained 540 days. KMS-wrapped keys control access; detailed KMS rotation schedule is in the control mapping sheet.
- Exception type column added as requested; we marked the three historical telemetry exceptions as 'config' (two) and 'operator' (one), each with compensating controls listed.

Next steps:
- Please confirm receipt. If this satisfies the technical team we will: 1) sign the attestation addendum and 2) open a secure artifact share (ASR) for any additional redacted samples you need.
- Karthik will follow up on the SOC 2 control ID crosswalk for CC6.2 and CC7.1 with explicit artifact names.

Thank you — happy to hop on a quick call if your reviewers want a 20-minute walkthrough.

Best,
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Attachments: network-dataflow-diagram.pdf; control-mapping-v2.xlsx; ingress-egress-exception-log.csv
